Insomnia and trying to fall asleep: I tried counting sheep, but I realized I'd been living with a herd all along.
Buying things you don't need online: I bought a $500 coffee maker online because I thought I needed it, but now I just use the one in my office and feel guilty every time.
Awkward family gatherings: I brought my dog to my aunt's house for Thanksgiving, and she asked if I had a "pet-friendly" relationship with my mom. I said, "She's not a pet, she's a roommate with a bad attitude."

Commuting in heavy traffic: I finally got a job that doesn't require me to commute, but now I'm stuck in traffic, which is basically the opposite of a job.
Job interviews: I once interviewed for a job that required me to "think on my feet." Turns out, they just wanted me to stand in a chair for 30 minutes.
Keeping houseplants alive: I bought a plant that came with a care guide — it said, "Water when the soil is dry." I checked the soil every day. It was never dry. I guess the plant was just waiting for me to panic.
Forgetting passwords: I tried to remember my password, but it slipped my mind — like a fish out of water.
High school reunions: I went to a high school reunion and realized I'd forgotten more about my ex than I remembered about myself.

Alarm clocks and waking up early: I bought an alarm clock that plays my favorite song — now I'm just waking up to my own voice.
The culture of social media influencers: Social media influencers are like modern-day shamans — they're not actually real, but people are paying money to follow their rituals.
Cryptocurrencies or \"Tech Bros\": Cryptocurrencies are like tech bros — they're all about the hype, the jargon, and the promise that one day, your $200 investment will be worth a million, even if it's just a digital version of a pizza.
Going to the dentist: I told my dentist I was scared of drills, and he said, "Don't worry, we don't use those anymore—just a little vibration and a lot of anxiety."
Moving to a new apartment: Moving to a new apartment is like starting a relationship — you're excited, you clean the place up, and then you realize you forgot to bring the dog.
Annoying neighbors: I finally got my neighbor to stop playing his guitar at 2 a.m. I told him, "You're not a rock star, you're a raccoon with a pick."
Overpacking for a vacation: I packed so much for my vacation, I brought a suitcase, a backpack, and a duffel bag — just in case the plane lost my luggage.
I downloaded a dating app to find love, but all I found was a dating app.
Public transportation/Subways: I tried to ride the subway without paying, but the conductor asked to see my ticket — and I had to explain I was just testing the system.
Wedding planning: I told my fiancé we'd keep the wedding small, but I didn't realize "small" meant 200 guests, a 10-foot cake, and a venue that charges by the square inch.
Autocorrect text message fails: I tried to text "I'm running late," but my autocorrect turned it into "I'm running late for my own funeral."
Procrastination: I tried to quit procrastinating, but my to-do list just kept getting longer. Turns out, the only thing I'm good at is delaying the inevitable.
Group chats that never stop buzzing: Group chats that never stop buzzing — you're always waiting for the next notification, but it's just your phone trying to tell you it's still alive.
The cost of living/Being broke: I tried to budget for the cost of living, but I realized I was just paying rent to a ghost.
Getting a bad haircut: I got a bad haircut, and now I look like a conspiracy theorist who's been through a blender.
Overly complicated modern fitness trends: I tried a "mindful movement" class where the instructor said, "Breathe in, then move your body like you're trying to escape a bear." I didn't realize the bear was in the room.
People who talk at the movie theater: People who talk at the movie theater are just trying to make sure the sound doesn't drown out their own voice.
Cooking disasters: I tried to make a soufflé once, and it turned out so bad, I had to call it "soufflé-ant."
Small talk about the weather: I always look forward to small talk about the weather — it's the only conversation where I can pretend I'm not a total stranger.
Modern fashion trends: I tried to wear a sweater this week, but it looked like I was dressed for a polar bear convention.
Waiting in doctors' offices: Waiting in a doctor's office is like being in a courtroom — you're always waiting for the verdict, but the judge is the one who's late.
Getting older/Turning 30: I used to think turning 30 was just a number, but now I realize it's the moment life hands you a calendar and says, "Here, pretend you're still 25."
Video game culture: I used to think video game culture was just about pixels and polygons — until I realized it's really just a bunch of people arguing about the same thing in different languages.
Corporate buzzwords (e.g., \"Synergy\"): Synergy isn't a word — it's a corporate conspiracy to make you think you're part of a team when you're just a spreadsheet with a title.
Dealing with landlords: You think you're dealing with a landlord, but in reality, you're just a tenant with a bad Google Maps suggestion.
Astrological signs/Horoscopes: I asked my friend if she believed in horoscopes, and she said, "I don't believe in them, but I do believe in the power of a good reading to make you feel seen."
People who overshare online: I once unfriended someone who posted a 10-page essay about their childhood trauma, and I’m still haunted by the fact that I read it in one sitting.
Veganism or extreme dietary restrictions: I've tried veganism, and let me tell you — it's like being a superhero, but the only powers you get are "no meat" and "no cheese."
Trying to assemble a tent/Camping: I bought a tent that came with a detailed instruction manual... and I followed it exactly — until I realized I was building a house.
